title: Preflight and Smoke Testing Patterns for Private VPC and Air‑Gapped Deployments
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This guide defines a pragmatic, repeatable preflight and smoke-testing pattern for Redwood private deployments (VPC-connected and air-gapped). It describes the test categories, minimal harness architecture, pass/fail criteria, operator runbook steps, and sample test configurations you can adapt for customer installs, upgrade canaries, and field handoffs. The intention is to catch critical failures before traffic is routed to customer workloads and to provide fast, actionable results during on-site or automated installs.

Scope and assumptions:

- Applies to private control‑plane installations (VPC + hybrid) and on‑prem air‑gapped appliances that host the Redwood inference runtime.
- Assumes base provisioning (compute, storage, network ACLs, KMS connectivity or local HSM) is complete.
- Focuses on verification of connectivity, security primitives, runtime liveness, model hot‑swap, KV cache sanity, telemetry, and a small representative workload (smoke).

Test categories (fast-to-run prioritized order):

1) Infrastructure & network preflight (2–10m)
- Validate DNS and service discovery resolution for control plane endpoints.
- Ensure required ports reachable (gRPC/TCP ranges, metrics, health endpoints).
- Confirm NTP sync (within 500ms drift) and MTU compatibility for RDMA if present.

2) Identity, secrets & attestation (1–5m)
- KMS/HSM connectivity check (API handshake + simple encrypt/decrypt).
- Certificate chain verification and expected SANs.
- TPM/attestation presence check for air‑gapped appliances.

3) Observability & telemetry (2–5m)
- Verify metrics scrape endpoint responds and Prometheus scrape succeeds.
- Confirm logs arrive to local aggregator (or configured remote endpoint) and include runtime version and model metadata.

4) Runtime basic health & liveness (2–10m)
- Service liveness /ready endpoints return healthy.
- KV cache read/write smoke (small key set).
- Model artifact existence check and checksum validation.

5) Model swap and inference smoke (5–15m) — the core smoke test
- Load a small, verified model (e.g., 7B-quality test artifact) into the runtime.
- Execute short generation (<64 tokens) and sampling requests to validate correctness and that outputs conform to structured form (if applicable).
- Validate latency and token emission (streaming) behavior under a single‑client load.

6) Throughput sanity + cold‑start spot check (5–20m)
- Run a short burst of synthetic requests to exercise batching and KV warm‑up paths.
- Measure cold‑start for a fresh worker (target: < 4s for model load on dedicated GPU for 7B; document-specific thresholds apply).

Pass/fail criteria (minimal):

- Any failure in categories 1–3: BLOCK (do not route customer traffic).
- Runtime liveness or model artifact checksum mismatch: BLOCK.
- Model smoke inference returns non‑empty output and passes basic schema checks: PASS.
- Latency SLOs: soft‑warning if 95th percentile exceeds configured threshold; BLOCK if median latency is > 2x expected for the confirmed target model profile.

Minimal harness architecture (pattern):

- Test runner (control): small container or operator CLI that orchestrates tests in sequence, collects artifacts, and emits a single pass/fail artifact.
- Local agents: lightweight scripts on control plane nodes or admin workstation that run network checks, KMS attestations, and trigger runtime calls.
- Synthetic workload store: canonical prompt/test vectors stored as versioned YAML/JSON in the distribution package.
- Results collector: writes a final JSON summary to /var/lib/redwood/validation-report.json and pushes to configured artifact storage when available.

Sample operator flow (numbered runbook):

1. Preflight: run network checks and report (run: redwood-preflight --check-ports --dns).
2. Secrets & attestation: execute kmstest --encrypt-test --verify-cert.
3. Observability: curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | head -n 10 and validate runtime_version label.
4. Runtime liveness: curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq .status and confirm "ok".
5. KV smoke: redwood-kv-test --set test:key "smoke" --get test:key --expect smoke.
6. Model deploy & swap: redwood-modelctl deploy --artifact /opt/artifacts/test-7b.tar.gz --name smoke-test-7b --wait 60
7. Inference smoke: redwood-client gen --model smoke-test-7b --input "Validate." --max-tokens 16 --stream --output /tmp/smoke-out.json
8. Throughput burst: redwood-loadtest --concurrency 8 --duration 30 --model smoke-test-7b --report /tmp/burst.json
9. Collect artifacts and evaluate pass/fail: redwood-validate --report /var/lib/redwood/validation-report.json --thresholds validation-thresholds.yaml

Example validation‑thresholds.yaml (as plain text table in this doc):

| metric | warning | block | notes |
|--------|---------|-------|-------|
| model_load_secs | 6 | 20 | for 7B on dedicated GPU; adjust per hardware |
| p95_latency_ms | 350 | 1000 | depends on sequence length and quantization |
| inference_success_rate | 0.98 | 0.95 | percent of requests that return a parsable response |
| telemetry_scrape_ok | true | false | Prometheus scrape and label presence |
| kms_roundtrip_ms | 200 | 2000 | warn if >200ms, block if unreachable |

Sample smoke test matrix (copy into your CI/test runner):

```
# columns: test_id, category, duration_secs, critical, command
smoke-001,network,30,true,redwood-preflight --check-ports --dns
smoke-002,kms,20,true,kmstest --encrypt-test --decrypt-test
smoke-003,observability,15,true,curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep runtime_version
smoke-004,kv,10,true,redwood-kv-test --set test:key smoke --get test:key
smoke-005,model-deploy,60,true,redwood-modelctl deploy --artifact /opt/artifacts/test-7b.tar.gz
smoke-006,inference,30,true,redwood-client gen --model smoke-test-7b --input "Hello" --max-tokens 16
smoke-007,throughput,45,false,redwood-loadtest --concurrency 4 --duration 30
```

Automated CI harness tips:

- Keep the smoke artifact small (test model < 100MB quantized stub or a distilled test artifact) to reduce pull time for air‑gapped installs.
- Version the test vectors and thresholds with the runtime package.
- Use idempotent test steps — tests should be re‑runnable without side effects.
- Capture and upload logs, kernel traces, and /proc/gpu stats on any non‑trivial failure.

Field operator quick checks (one‑liner cheatsheet):

- DNS: dig +short controlplane.redwood.internal | head -n1
- Certs: openssl s_client -connect kms.customer.local:443 -showcerts
- Metrics: curl -sS http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep -E "runtime_version|model_"
- KV: redwood-kv-test --set smoke:ok ok --get smoke:ok

Rollforward/rollback triggers tied to preflight results:

- Immediate rollback (do not route traffic) if: KMS unavailable; certificate validation fails; runtime liveness is false; model artifact checksum mismatch.
- Conditional rollforward (postpone customer traffic until resolved) if: telemetry scrape labels missing; p95 latency above warning but below block threshold — escalate to SRE and place under a limited traffic policy (10% or rate‑limited).

Ownership and SLAs:

- Ownership: deployment engineer owns preflight, SRE owns runbook for escalations, and customer success is notified for any BLOCK.
- Evidence retention: keep validation artifacts for 30 days in customer‑scoped bucket.
- Delivery SLA for critical failures found in preflight: respond within 2 business hours; mitigation plan in 24 hours.

Operational notes and gotchas:

- Air‑gapped installs: test artifact distribution must be cryptographically signed and checksummed; validate signatures before deploy.
- KV cache warm‑up: expected higher first‑request latency — include warm‑up step in preflight.
- Hardware heterogeneity: define a hardware profile label and adjust thresholds per profile.

Appendix — sample minimal YAML test definition (paste into your runner):

```yaml
version: 1
name: preflight-smoke-suite
tests:
  - id: network
    critical: true
    run: redwood-preflight --check-ports --dns
  - id: kms
    critical: true
    run: kmstest --encrypt-test --decrypt-test
  - id: model_smoke
    critical: true
    run: |
      redwood-modelctl deploy --artifact /opt/artifacts/test-7b.tar.gz --name smoke-test-7b --wait 60
      redwood-client gen --model smoke-test-7b --input "Smoke" --max-tokens 16 --output /tmp/smoke.json
  - id: burst
    critical: false
    run: redwood-loadtest --concurrency 4 --duration 30
report:
  path: /var/lib/redwood/validation-report.json
  upload_on_success: false
```
